vulnerability.category_l2: CRLF injection: a quoted-string local part containing raw line breaks survives address validation and is emitted into mail headers and SMTP MAIL FROM/RCPT TO commands

critical_operation.description: Address::__construct is documented as the validation boundary for every Mailer address. It trims the address, strips CR/LF from the display name, and then treats EmailValidator::isValid with RFCValidation as sufficient. A local part written as an RFC-5322 quoted string can contain raw CRLF bytes, which that validator accepts, so the value is stored verbatim. Address::getEncodedAddress() goes through IdnAddressEncoder, which leaves the local part untouched, and the value is later inserted into rendered headers and into sprintf("MAIL FROM:<%s>\r\n") / sprintf("RCPT TO:<%s>\r\n"), so the embedded CRLF starts a new header or SMTP command. The 5.4.52 fix adds a rejection of any address containing bytes in [\x00-\x1F\x7F].

entry_point.description: Application code constructs an Address from a user-influenced string, for example a contact form "from" or "reply-to" field, or passes it to Envelope. The constructor is the only gate between that input and the transport.

trace.description: Application passes a user-supplied address to the constructor; trim() does not remove interior CRLF
the validator accepts the quoted-string local part with embedded CRLF, so the address is stored
getEncodedAddress leaves the local part untouched, preserving the control bytes
the SMTP transport formats the address into MAIL FROM/RCPT TO command lines, so CRLF starts a new command

supports: encodeString splits at the last @, re-encodes only the domain when it contains non-ASCII characters, and returns the local part untouched
getEncodedAddress therefore preserves raw CRLF bytes embedded in a quoted-string local part
doSend() passes $envelope->getSender()->getEncodedAddress() and each recipient getEncodedAddress() to the SMTP command helpers
doMailFromCommand() formats "MAIL FROM:<%s>\r\n" and doRcptToCommand() formats "RCPT TO:<%s>\r\n" with the address inserted verbatim
a CRLF inside the address therefore terminates the SMTP command and starts an attacker-chosen one
getBodyAsString() starts from $this->address->getEncodedAddress() and appends the display name
the address string is emitted into the rendered header without stripping control characters
each address is serialized with getEncodedAddress() before being joined into the header body
no control-character filtering happens at this layer
the file opens with a PHP open tag and declares namespace Symfony\Component\Mime
the snapshot inventory records the Mime component as PHP

source_crosscheck.notes: All sources agree on CWE-93, the CRLF-in-quoted-string mechanism, the <5.4.52 range and the v5.4.52 release. The GHSA body and symfony.com both print a dead 5.4 fix commit dc2dbd29; the CNA reference a1c42cbe resolves and matches the resolution text and the diff. NVD is still Awaiting Analysis, has no CPE configuration, and carries only the CNA 4.0 6.3 vector as a Secondary metric. GHSA labels the issue HIGH although the published score is 6.3 Medium.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read Address::__construct at v5.4.45 and confirm there is no control-character rejection before the validator call.
An independent reviewer must confirm the quoted-string example is accepted by the validator path being used, or record that only the advisory asserts it.
An independent reviewer must confirm a1c42cbe is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.52, and that dc2dbd29 does not exist.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range includes 5.4.45 and the fixed release is 5.4.52.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No PHP runtime, egulias validator, Symfony Mailer or SMTP server was executed; the finding is static.
Acceptance of "x\r\nBcc: attacker@evil"@example.com by egulias EmailValidator is asserted by the advisory and its regression test provider; the library behavior itself was not executed.
Exploitability requires application code to accept a user-controlled address; no specific application was tested.
Only the 5.4 branch was fetched and compared; 6.4.40, 7.4.12 and 8.0.12 were not diffed.
NVD status is Awaiting Analysis with no CPE configuration; the 6.3 MEDIUM score is the CNA vector republished as Secondary. GHSA labels it HIGH, which disagrees with the score.
open_questions: Whether the installed egulias version in the snapshot accepts the exact quoted-string example was not executed.
Which header builders are reached in a given Mailer configuration (MailboxHeader versus MailboxListHeader) depends on how the application sets the address.
